Moderately positive but cautious. The hike to 1–1.25% and the intent to begin balance-sheet normalization convey a rule-like, gradual tightening consistent with Taylor-style reaction functions and interest-rate smoothing found in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler and in Taylor’s work. Yet with inflation running below 2% and market-based inflation compensation still low, the tone aligns with inflation-forecast targeting and expectations management emphasized by Svensson and Woodford, as well as term-structure evidence that inflation expectations remain subdued (e.g., Ang and Piazzesi). Forward guidance that the funds rate will stay below its longer-run level, plus the symmetric 2% goal, further reflects the literature’s case for gradualism (Woodford; Goodfriend on operating frameworks). The Kashkari dissent highlights internal caution about disinflation risks. Net effect: slightly less upbeat than a pure “hawkish” read.
